cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Hungry – having a strong, continuous desire or craving for something (like learning or goals).

p.em: Example: To achieve great milestones, you must stay hungry for knowledge and never settle.

cosy-blockquote.p: Foolish – willing to take major risks or make choices that others might think are unwise or bizarre.

p.em: Example: Staying foolish means being brave enough to try things that traditional experts think are impossible.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ambition – a strong desire to do or achieve something great through dedication and hard work.

p.em: Example: His initial ambition was simple, but his continuous curiosity led to a massive tech revolution.

cosy-blockquote.p: Curiosity – a strong, passionate desire to know, explore, or learn about things.

p.em: Example: It was his endless curiosity about design and calligraphy that shaped the typography of early computers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unconventional – not based on or conforming to what is generally done, accepted, or believed.

p.em: Example: He was famous for his unconventional habits, like walking barefoot around the office.

cosy-blockquote.p: Perseverance – persistence in doing something despite extreme difficulty, delays, or failure.

p.em: Example: It took years of intense perseverance to rebuild the company after being dismissed.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intuition – the ability to understand or decide something immediately using your gut feeling rather than conscious logic.

p.em: Example: He advised students to have the courage to follow their heart and intuition.

cosy-blockquote.p: Visionary – a person with original, highly creative, and imaginative ideas about what the future will be like.

p.em: Example: A true visionary does not create what clients want today, but what they will love tomorrow.

cosy-blockquote.p: Invention – the action of inventing something, or a unique new process or device.

p.em: Example: True invention requires a willingness to make many mistakes along the way.

cosy-blockquote.p: Risk-taking – the act of taking actions which might result in failure but are necessary to achieve something great.

p.em: Example: Without a healthy attitude toward risk-taking, an entrepreneur will remain stuck in ordinary routines.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What do you think Steve Jobs meant by "stay foolish", and why is healthy risk-taking so essential for success?
★ Have you ever made a choice that others thought was foolish, but turned out to be correct?

Why is it important to stay hungry for knowledge even after achieving your initial goals?
★ What is one project or skill that you are currently hungry to master?

How does the fear of failure prevent people from following their gut intuition?
★ When was the last time you ignored logic to follow your own intuition?

Why are highly visionary ideas often rejected by traditional experts at the beginning?
★ Do you consider yourself a dreamer with a big future vision, or a practical person?

In what ways does constant, stubborn perseverance outweigh natural talent in building a business?
★ What is the hardest obstacle you have managed to overcome through pure perseverance?

Why is an unconventional career path often far more rewarding than a traditional, safe one?
★ What is the most unconventional habit or routine that helps you stay productive?

How does intellectual curiosity prevent our daily minds from becoming lazy and ordinary?
★ What narrow, unusual topic has sparked your curiosity recently?

Why does a great technological invention require us to tolerate a high level of uncertainty?
★ If you could create any new invention to make daily life simpler, what would it do?

How does having strong personal ambition help you stay focused during periods of doubt?
★ How has your personal ambition shifted or evolved over the last five years?

Can a person stay true to their own path if they never engage in active risk-taking?
★ If you had to describe your attitude toward risk-taking in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: Which mindset profile is most likely to produce a ground-breaking visionary in the modern era? Rank them: - 🚀 The Passionate Innovator Possesses endless curiosity, values invention, and relies on intuition to design unconventional tools. - 🛡️ The Disciplined Builder Shows immense perseverance, avoids risk-taking, but builds stable, long-lasting products systematically. - 🌀 The Foolish Dreamer Constantly hungry for change, engages in wild risk-taking, and rejects any traditional business model. - 💼 The Strategic Visionary Balances high ambition with deep intuition, executing carefully calculated risks with absolute focus.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will allow us to measure a person's level of curiosity and focus in real time. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if school algorithms began to filter and monitor your individual ambition?

Modern digital screens will eventually destroy our collective capacity for deep perseverance and gut intuition. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use brain-boosting chips to artificially stay hungry for learning?

Future societies will completely ban standardized exams, letting children learn purely based on unconventional methods. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think future kids will be more willing to take foolish risks than today's children?

As artificial intelligence advances, humans will not need to focus on any traditional invention. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What is one simple human invention you hope we never lose?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our willingness to engage in bold space risk-taking. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where traditional careers are fully automated?

In the coming decades, a truly visionary leader will be selected by software predictions rather than voting. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about the power of intuition to people 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true unconventional lifestyles incredibly difficult to maintain. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic city that guarantees physical safety at the cost of your risk-taking?

In the future, social status will be determined by how hungry a person is for growth rather than their family wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope personal intuition will play in your own professional future over the next decade?

One day, being passionately curious and foolish will be seen as the single most valuable trait of any worker. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to show greater ambition right now?

A world fully governed by smart algorithms will have no space left for the quiet mystery of human invention. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If an app could make you very successful, would you still listen to your intuition?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
